name: TVT vs PAHG
question: Is polyacrylamide hydrogel injection noninferior to retropubic tension-free vaginal tape for patient satisfaction in women with primary stress urinary incontinence?

design.population: Women with primary stress urinary incontinence unresponsive to conservative treatment, a positive cough stress test without urge-type leakage and no previous incontinence procedure.

verdictNote: Hydrogel missed the 20% satisfaction margin at 1, 3 and 5 years; complications were fewer after hydrogel.
takeaway: Polyacrylamide hydrogel (Bulkamid) injection was compared with retropubic tension-free vaginal tape in women with primary stress incontinence; 1-year satisfaction of at least 80/100 was 59.8% versus 95.0%, missing the 20% noninferiority limit, while most perioperative complications and all six complication-related reoperations followed tape.

reports.label: 1-year primary report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed entrez date (Crossref record created 2019-09-03); issue date February 2020
reports.citation: Itkonen Freitas AM, Mentula M, Rahkola-Soisalo P, Tulokas S, Mikkola TS. Tension-free vaginal tape surgery versus polyacrylamide hydrogel injection for primary stress urinary incontinence: a randomized clinical trial. *J Urol.* 2020;203(2):372-378.

results.measure: 1-year patient satisfaction of at least 80/100 on a visual analogue scale; risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points
results.note: Intention-to-treat among the 208 women who attended (101 TVT, 107 hydrogel); hydrogel did not meet the prespecified 20% noninferiority limit. Median satisfaction 99 (IQR 94 to 100) versus 85 (IQR 65 to 98).

results.measure: Negative cough stress test at 1 year; risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points
results.note: Denominators not given in the abstract.

harms.label: Perioperative complications (cases cited in the abstract)
harms.note: The abstract states that most perioperative complications, including 19 TVT versus 3 hydrogel cases (difference 16.0%, 95% CI 7.8-24.9), were associated with TVT; denominators are not given.

harms.label: Reoperations due to complications
harms.note: All 6 reoperations were associated with TVT (difference 5.9%, 95% CI 1.2-12.4); denominators are not given.

delivery.label: Women entering the trial
delivery.note: 224 women entered between September 28, 2015 and March 1, 2017. Later reports count 223 randomized (TVT 110, hydrogel 113).

reports.label: 1-year quality of life and sexual function
reports.citation: Itkonen Freitas AM, Mikkola TS, Rahkola-Soisalo P, Tulokas S, Mentula M. Quality of life and sexual function after TVT surgery versus Bulkamid injection for primary stress urinary incontinence: 1 year results from a randomized clinical trial. *Int Urogynecol J.* 2021;32(3):595-601.
reports.followUp: 1 year; UDI-6 and IIQ-7 completed by 103 of 104 TVT and 108 of 108 hydrogel women

results.measure: 1-year mean UDI-6 total score (0-100, higher is worse distress; baseline 34.57 hydrogel, 31.48 TVT)
results.note: Both groups improved from baseline; between-group p value as printed. Secondary analysis of a trial powered for satisfaction.

results.measure: Women reaching at least 75% improvement in UDI-6 at 1 year
results.note: The 75% threshold is borrowed from a minimally important difference used for the ICIQ-UI-SF; none is defined for the UDI-6.

results.measure: Women reaching at least 75% improvement in IIQ-7 at 1 year

delivery.label: Treated as randomized and analyzed
delivery.note: Six TVT and five hydrogel women withdrew consent after randomization, one woman accidentally received two randomization envelopes and four were lost to follow-up.

reports.label: 3-year follow-up
reports.citation: Itkonen Freitas AM, Isaksson C, Rahkola-Soisalo P, Tulokas S, Mentula M, Mikkola TS. Tension-free vaginal tape and polyacrylamide hydrogel injection for primary stress urinary incontinence: 3-year followup from a randomized clinical trial. *J Urol.* 2022;208(3):658-667.

results.measure: 3-year satisfaction of at least 80/100; risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points
results.note: Intention-to-treat among attenders; hydrogel did not meet the prespecified 20% noninferiority limit.

results.measure: Would come again for the treatment; risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points
Negative cough stress test at 3 years; risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points
results.note: Abstract and text give the interval 8.6-26.9; Table 2 prints 8.0-27.2.

results.measure: Both cough stress test and pad test negative at 3 years (intention to treat); risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points
results.note: Percentages as printed; 50.0% implies a hydrogel denominator of 94 rather than 96.

results.measure: Symptoms cured on a 5-point Likert scale at 3 years; risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points
Symptoms cured or improved at 3 years; risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points

results.endpoint: Cough stress and pad test, per protocol
results.measure: Both tests negative at 3 years, treatment-received analysis excluding crossover; risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points

harms.label: Any peri- or postoperative complication before crossover
harms.note: Difference 19.5 percentage points (95% CI 6.8-31.4) in the 3-year attenders.

harms.label: Perioperative complications
harms.note: Before crossover. TVT: bladder perforation 7/104 (6.7%), hematoma 6/104 (5.8%), acute retention 10/104 (9.6%); hydrogel: acute retention 2/108 (1.9%), no perforation or hematoma.

harms.label: Vaginal tape erosion between 3 months and 3 years
harms.note: Before crossover; reoperation due to erosion in 3/92 (3.3%). None of the women had the sling removed.

harms.label: Reoperation for a complication
harms.note: TVT: hematoma 1, retention 3, erosion 3. Hydrogel: pain 1 (hydrogel removal under general anesthesia for persisting pain and dysuria, requested about 20 months after injection; the pain did not change), fibrotic resistance at the bladder neck 1 (aspiration under local anesthesia). Denominators not stated for this count.

harms.label: Tape or implantation-site pain
harms.note: Between 3 months and 3 years, before crossover; median numerical rating 3 (interquartile range 2-4) among those reporting pain at 3 years.

harms.label: De novo urgency requiring medication
harms.note: Between 3 months and 3 years, before crossover.

harms.label: Complications after crossover from hydrogel to TVT
harms.note: Among the 30 hydrogel women who crossed over to TVT: 2 reoperations (hematoma, tape loosening), 1 erosion, 1 tape-site pain, 3 dysuria, 2 retention and 3 de novo urgency.

harms.label: Clavien-Dindo grade III
harms.note: Grade IV: 1/92 (1.1%) after TVT (ischemic heart symptoms possibly related to local anesthesia) and none after hydrogel.

delivery.label: Crossover by 3 years

values.exp: 30/96 to TVT (16 before and 14 after the 1-year visit)

delivery.note: No woman had a second TVT.

delivery.label: Hydrogel injections received by 3 years
delivery.value: 1 injection only 31/96 (32.3%); 2 injections 35/96 (36.5%); TVT after 1 injection 15/96 (15.6%); TVT after 2 injections 15/96 (15.6%)
delivery.note: A top-up injection at the 3-month visit was part of the protocol for persisting symptoms.

delivery.label: Operators
delivery.value: Nine urogynecologists performed TVT; two performed hydrogel injections

delivery.label: Setting and anesthesia
delivery.value: Outpatient, local anesthesia for both: TVT-Exact with 70-100 mL of 0.25% prilocaine with epinephrine; Bulkamid with 10 mL periurethral lidocaine

delivery.label: Hydrogel injection technique
delivery.value: Endoscopic injection 1.5 cm from the vesicourethral junction at 10, 2, 5 and 7 o'clock

delivery.label: Discharge criteria
delivery.value: Successful micturition and post-void residual below 200 mL

reports.citation: Itkonen Freitas AM, Isaksson C, Rahkola-Soisalo P, Mentula M, Mikkola TS. reports.followUp: 3 years; questionnaires adequately completed by 94 TVT and 96 hydrogel women

results.measure: 3-year mean UDI-6 total score (0-100, higher is worse distress; baseline 34.57 hydrogel, 31.48 TVT); between-group mean difference (TVT minus hydrogel)
3-year mean IIQ-7 total score (0-100, higher is worse impact; baseline 54.50 hydrogel, 50.79 TVT); between-group mean difference (TVT minus hydrogel)

delivery.label: Women in the 3-year questionnaire analysis
delivery.note: Of 212 treated as randomized (TVT 104, hydrogel 108). By 3 years 30 hydrogel women (31.3%) had crossed over to TVT and 3 TVT women (3.2%) had received hydrogel; the analysis is intention to treat.

reports.label: 5-year follow-up
reports.citation: Itkonen Freitas AM, Isaksson C, Rahkola-Soisalo P, Mentula M, Mikkola TS. Tension-free vaginal tape versus polyacrylamide hydrogel injection for stress urinary incontinence: 5-year follow-up. *NEJM Evid.* 2025;4(5):EVIDoa2400216.

results.measure: 5-year satisfaction of at least 80/100; risk difference (TVT minus hydrogel), percentage points
results.note: Hydrogel did not meet the prespecified 20% noninferiority criterion. The abstract gives counts and percentages without denominators (195 attenders; 99 and 96 implied by the percentages).

harms.label: Peri- or postoperative complication before crossover
harms.note: Difference 21.5 percentage points (95% CI 8.4-33.8); the abstract states that complications were twice as common in the TVT group. Denominators implied by the percentages are 99 and 96.

delivery.label: Randomized, treated as randomized, attended at 5 years
delivery.note: Per-arm attendance is implied by the percentages in the abstract (hydrogel 99, TVT 96).
